questions: Which conservative positive discretizations of electron-impact ionization preserve electron number and total kinetic plus ionization energy when the two outgoing daughter electrons are deposited onto a finite energy grid?

How do kinetic and thermal electron models conserve particle number and energy when their separation energy depends on temperature, and what implicit temperature closure or moving-boundary effective heat capacity is derived?

search_summary.scope: Targeted conservation and thermalization comparison; no exhaustive audit or global novelty claim

retrieval_observations.observation: Several results concern semiconductor, quantum or unrelated plasma-temperature models. These are not used as evidence for a moving kinetic/thermal cutoff.
SciSpace returned repository and journal duplicates, including repository dates differing from original publication. Original arXiv/publisher dates and titles determine source identity.
The fetched Le–Cambier ar5iv page displays August 8, 2026. Original arXiv submission and journal reference both identify the 2017 paper; displayed page date is not used as publication date.
Exa text retrieval was bounded at 90000 or 75000 characters per URL. Only the explicitly listed complete passages were treated as read; no claim of reading all benchmark sections or appendices.

scope_exclusions: No source read here supplies the candidate-specific sharp E_c(T) effective-heat-capacity theorem. That is a direct-proof obligation, not a literature-wide absence claim.
Landau elastic discretizations and moving-velocity meshes found during discovery were not pursued because the four selected sources suffice for this narrow comparison.

candidate_review.scope: Four primary comparisons are contextual. Candidate proofs/code were independently read; no global novelty or new no-go theorem is adopted.
